title: Independence of the row projections of a Rademacher matrix
statement: Fix natural numbers $k$ and $d$, and let the entries of a $k \times d$ matrix be drawn independently from the Rademacher distribution and each scaled by $1/\sqrt{k}$, giving a random matrix $A(\omega) \in \bbr^{k \times d}$ whose sample $\omega$ is distributed according to the joint Rademacher product measure. Then for every fixed vector $x \in \bbr^{d}$, the $k$ real-valued random variables $\omega \mapsto \bigl(A(\omega)\,x\bigr)_i$, one for each row index $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$, are mutually independent.
hypotheses_covered: k and d are natural numbers
x is a fixed vector in R^d
omega is distributed according to the joint Rademacher product measure
conclusion ranges over all k row indices i
replaced:
For any $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$, the $k$ row projections
$i \mapsto (A(\omega)\,x)_i$ are mutually independent random variables under
the joint Rademacher measure.
